title: Commit to an orchestration boundary
description: Select a workload and architecture. The execution map reveals whether the design adds unnecessary autonomy or omits required durable state.

architectures.label: Deterministic pipeline
architectures.detail: A fixed sequence of typed stages with no model-controlled tool routing.

architectures.label: Bounded LangChain agent
architectures.detail: A model chooses among approved tools inside an iteration and deadline budget.

architectures.label: Custom LangGraph
architectures.detail: Explicit nodes and transitions with checkpoints, interrupts, and resumable branches.
architectures.controlModel: Graph owns transitions and resume points

scenarios.label: Invoice extraction
scenarios.brief: Validate one document, extract a known schema, and reject unsupported fields.

pipeline.explanation: The path is known before execution, so typed stages preserve the simplest test and failure model.

agent.explanation: Tool choice adds a probabilistic branch even though the required sequence is already known.
missing: A product reason for model-controlled routing

graph.explanation: The graph is correct but introduces checkpoint and migration work without a pause or recovery requirement.

scenarios.label: Support research
scenarios.brief: Choose among read-only account, order, and policy tools to answer a customer's question.

pipeline.explanation: A fixed pipeline must call every source or encode a growing decision tree outside the model.

agent.explanation: The agent can select approved read tools while the runtime bounds iterations, deadline, and output.

graph.explanation: A graph can contain the agent, but durable branching does not yet solve an additional requirement.
missing: A long-running or explicit branching need

scenarios.label: Refund approval
scenarios.brief: Investigate an order, pause for human approval, issue a refund, and resume after a worker restart.

pipeline.explanation: One request handler cannot safely wait across approval latency and deployment restarts without external workflow state.

agent.explanation: An agent loop can investigate, but messages alone do not define a durable business transition or safe refund replay.

graph.explanation: Checkpoints and interrupts make the approval and effect boundaries explicit and resumable.

scenarios.label: Incident remediation
scenarios.brief: Fan out diagnostics, compare evidence, require approval, then execute one reversible change.

pipeline.explanation: A linear chain obscures parallel evidence and cannot express a durable approval boundary cleanly.

agent.explanation: The agent can choose diagnostics, but the high-impact transition still needs explicit orchestration and recovery.

graph.explanation: The graph exposes parallel collection, evidence convergence, approval, and a reversible action as separate states.
